Instead they get an explicit Graveyard entry, which states what programmes close and points to those two cards, plus Chains and Not-a-finding pointers.

It loads B's cookies with the attributes from their real Set-Cookie lines (new file `$E/accounts/B.set-cookie`, captured in CSR-001 step 1), waits out Chromium's two-minute Lax+POST window, serves the proof page itself from 127.0.0.1, and logs which cookies and which Origin and Referer each request to the target carried.

Offline checks (no network): all 14 bash blocks pass bash -n and the real scripts/scope_guard.py against a throwaway engagement in the scratchpad. Negative controls confirmed that engagement blocks a foreign host and a missing programme header. The harness was run only against a Playwright stub, never a real browser.

The guard check caught one real problem, now fixed: `python3 -m http.server` next to a curl POST is blocked, because the guard reads `http.server` as a host. xxe.md line 202 has the same server command, but I did not check whether it sits next to a POST there.

Decisions to review:
- Applies when is `http`, not the brief's `http, app|api`. Path redirects (RDR-003, gated `!default-page`) and cached header redirects (RDR-010, gated `cache`) happen on static and redirect-only hosts too; #380760 is one. Every parameter card still requires `redirect-param`, which needs app|api.
- The five discovery cards (RDR-001 to RDR-005) have `—` in Excluded by instead of `open-redirect`. Otherwise the planner would close them on most programmes and RDR-006 to RDR-009 would never get the redirects they need. The Graveyard explains this, and the cards say to park the result and report only a chain. The cost: `sane gate` will not stop a standalone open-redirect report against those cards on a programme that excludes the class.
- RDR-006 overlaps XSS-004 and RDR-008 overlaps OAU-002. Both cards say to reuse the other card's outcome and report one root cause once.

Every bash block parses. Each one also ran against a local fake curl, with no network requests. That run found and I fixed two bugs: a tab that a bypass puts into Location broke the RDR-002 and RDR-003 verdicts, and a one-letter variable in RDR-008 could collide with the operator's shell. The Playwright scripts are syntax-checked only, because Playwright is not installed here. A few values the hunter must fill in remain as `<...>` (A's sign-in credentials, the captured OAuth code), as authn.md and oauth.md already do.

claim-accounts (capability): the operator holds accounts at the hosting, cloud, DNS, mail and registrar services a claim needs (AWS, Azure, GitHub, Heroku, Mailgun, a registrar). STO-003, STO-005, STO-006 and STO-009 need them, and without the tag the planner cannot list those claims as blocked.

mx-3p (asset): a name's MX records point at a third-party mail service or at a host that does not resolve. No host fact covers this, so STO-006 runs once per programme as a sweep over every name instead of as a host card.
cloud-ip (asset): a name's A records are addresses from a public cloud provider's pool. No host fact covers this, so STO-007 runs as an ungated (`—`) once-per-programme sweep.
